archetypes.summary: A build-time application with no authoritative runtime service.
use_when: Content or assets can be produced ahead of time
No server-owned mutable state is required
reject_when: Secrets must be held by a server

archetypes.summary: One independently deployable service exposing a synchronous API.
use_when: One team owns one cohesive server capability
reject_when: Multiple services have no distinct ownership or scaling reason
defaults: One primary persistence boundary at most

archetypes.summary: One deployable application with enforced internal module boundaries.
use_when: Several business capabilities must evolve together
A small team needs simple deployment
reject_when: Independent deployment is already a proven requirement

archetypes.summary: A browser client, one server API, and one primary database.
use_when: Interactive browser UX and server-owned state are both required
reject_when: There is no server-owned state or secret

archetypes.summary: A bounded asynchronous processor consuming durable work items.
use_when: Retries or long-running processing are required
reject_when: A synchronous call satisfies latency and reliability

archetypes.summary: A command-line program or local automation with explicit inputs and outputs.
use_when: Local or CI execution is sufficient
reject_when: Nontechnical users require a graphical interface

archetypes.summary: A reusable package embedded into another process.
use_when: Consumers need an API rather than a standalone application
reject_when: The project owns an operational runtime
No stable consumer contract can be defined

archetypes.summary: A repeatable ingestion, transformation, validation, and publication flow.
reject_when: The main interaction is transactional CRUD

archetypes.summary: An engine-hosted extension with strict runtime-side and asset boundaries.
use_when: A host engine owns lifecycle, rendering, or simulation
reject_when: The project is a standalone application
The engine and version are not pinned
